hot.title: A Survey on Continuous Diffusion and Flow Language Models
hot.summary: The authors survey continuous language models for parallel, few-step text generation, explaining how shared sequence flows couple token positions and how learned flow maps make finite jumps. They contrast this with independent marginal sampling and discuss RePlaid’s training-compute gap: 20× with self-conditioning, down from Plaid’s 64×. Scaling matched discrete diffusion over the evaluated compute range; practical efficiency remains open.

hot.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
hot.summary: The authors survey mechanistic interpretability as a way to study models’ internal representations and computations, using causal interventions to test explanations. They propose evaluating analyses for attribution faithfulness, completeness, stability, causal validity, and human interpretability. In a constructed sleeper-agent model, a linear probe decoded trigger state with >99% AUROC, demonstrating decodability, not causal understanding or a safety guarantee.

hot.title: Embodied First Exam
hot.summary: The Embodied First Exam (EFE) evaluates coding agents controlling robots across direct control, controller-writing, and policy-training approaches. It standardizes tasks, information access, resources, and external verification across 1,156 tasks, 35 suites, and 47 robots. On 391 paired core tasks, GPT-6 Astra solved 30% in Standard and 77% in Privileged; these simulated results compare access conditions, not real-world readiness.

hot.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
hot.summary: The authors present Sage-Taiyi, a research system that tracks evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, and scope to guide which targets and reasoning methods to pursue. In expert-guided cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation, condition optimization raised isolated yield from trace to 84%. On Taiyi-Bench, Sage-Taiyi scored 53.95 versus 47.85 for AI Scientist-v2; this full-system comparison does not isolate monitoring’s contribution.

hot.summary: The Ultimate MoE Training Handbook is a practical guide to designing, training, profiling, and serving mixture-of-experts models, with runnable Megatron-LM recipes and monitoring methods. It compares a 1.22B-parameter dense baseline with a 6.86B-parameter MoE model that activates about 1.22B parameters per token, and combines cluster experiments with findings from published model reports. hot.title: FlashState: Unlocking Flexible Hybrid State Management for Agentic LLM Serving
hot.summary: The authors introduce FlashState, which captures matching attention and recurrent state at an agent request’s endpoint and selectively retains complete states under cache pressure. In a 48-session coding-agent replay with GLM-5.3-Flash, 1M-token context, and two NVIDIA B200 GPUs per engine, it achieved 4.66M prefill tokens per minute per GPU versus 1.48M for vLLM, about 3.14×, in that setup.

hot.title: ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use
hot.summary: ToolDex records full hand–tool–target interactions, including deformable targets, using synchronized egocentric and exocentric views with annotations for hands, tools, and targets. It pairs demonstrations with benchmarks for reasoning, reconstruction, and robot policies. Across six simulated tasks, Dex-X reinforcement learning averages 55.1% success versus 14.0% for kinematic retargeting and 4.6% for behavior cloning, not real-world performance.

hot.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
hot.summary: Agency inserts an interposition layer between harnesses, models, and tools to reduce context and calls. Its techniques compact context, remove stale history, search metadata, and batch calls. Across 200 tasks, four models, and three harnesses, they average 0.77 of baseline cost and 0.97 of baseline accuracy, though some tasks cost more and accuracy declines on some OfficeQA tasks.

hot.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
hot.summary: SwarmEvolve uses many agents to search for scientific and mathematical programs, sharing internal model memories instead of lengthy text. A synthesizer writes candidate programs, which an evaluator scores. Across 21 problems, Qwen3 8B averaged 0.804, versus CodeEvolve’s 0.700, in 60-minute runs. Its median time to reach OpenEvolve’s 60-minute score was 7 minutes, a time-to-target result, not a universal win.

hot.title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
hot.summary: The paper introduces selective self-distillation (SSD), training a model to answer using context-informed teacher guidance. SSD uses the teacher’s next token when its prediction differs from the student’s beyond a threshold, while applying distillation loss at every response position. Across three QA tasks, it uses 38–69% fewer supervised tokens than on-policy training, with accuracy within 1.4 percentage points except on Company Memo.

hot.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
hot.summary: EBR gives recurrent reasoning a learned energy score to guide hidden-state updates toward lower energy; its gradient also ranks candidate answers and signals when to stop. On Sudoku-Extreme, it reaches 99.92% exact accuracy at 0.61 TFLOPs per puzzle, versus EqR's 99.8% at about 210 TFLOPs, comparing inference compute, not elapsed time. Evidence covers structured algorithmic benchmarks, not general language reasoning.

hot.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
hot.summary: Video-Coder uses a coding agent to build and render an executable 3D scene, then guides a video generator with the draft. The agent can inspect execution feedback and frames and revise its code. With MiniMax-H3, it scores 0.67 versus 0.61 on PhyGenBench and 78.19% versus 54.58% on VBench-2.0 physical dimensions; its material score remains below CogVideoX-1.5’s 83.19%. These benchmark results cover tested settings.

hot.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
hot.summary: The authors study monitor-based interventions against reward hacking in Qwen3-4B across three task settings. They compare probes and judges with synthetic monitors whose errors are randomized, and test penalty designs. Synthetic monitors can outperform realistic monitors despite lower initial accuracy. A medical judge reduced test-set hacking by 22.4 percentage points with a 0.3-point performance increase, but no intervention eliminated hacking without performance costs across the study.

hot.title: Quantum-geometry-controlled pseudogap and non-Fermi-liquid behavior
hot.summary: Authors calculate geometry effects on pairing fluctuations and normal-state spectra in two-band models. They vary the quantum metric at fixed band energies, using a multiorbital T-matrix approximation. Larger metric weakens the calculated pseudogap in flat-band models and accompanies increasingly Fermi-liquid-like spectra in a dispersive model. The authors interpret this as a BEC-like-to-BCS-like crossover, not a measured material transition.

hot.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
hot.summary: VFlash generates spatial plans for vision-language models by drafting complete structured primitives, such as trajectories, in parallel, while retaining target-verified decoding for text. On MolmoSpaces, a world action model using VFlash plans reaches 70.2% success versus 61.0% with autoregressive plans. On Jetson Thor, batch-one model-pipeline latency is 703.3 ms versus 3,552.7 ms; this is not full robot response time.

hot.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
hot.summary: WorldFoundry defines a world model by a loop in which a system maintains state from interaction history, predicts action effects, and revises state from new observations, then provides contracts for running and evaluating systems while preserving native semantics. Its catalog lists 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 metric entries; one OpenVLA task succeeds in 179 steps, while two reach 520-step limits.

hot.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
hot.summary: The authors present a workflow in which agents propose quantum programs and Lean checks proofs of correctness and resource costs against fixed specifications. For warm-dense-hydrogen stopping power, the verified solution reduces estimated logical spacetime cost from 5.42×10^15 to 4.98×10^14, or 10.9×, under the stated model; it was not run on quantum hardware.

hot.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
hot.summary: AMP1 lets a general-purpose model control robot manipulation through code that observes the scene, commands motion, checks outcomes, and revises actions. It stays involved as tasks unfold, rather than relying on skill menus or programs without feedback. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 with Gemini 4 Argon succeeds in 85.6% of episodes; physical trials cover one single-arm Franka setup, and the system is slow.

hot.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
hot.summary: WorkflowArena evaluates how models organize long-horizon tasks by choosing whether and how to delegate, recording workflows alongside deliverables across 145 tasks in eight domains. In a fixed-executor transfer test, Kimi scores 45.04 with static workflows authored by Opus and 29.69 with those authored by Astra. Overall Resolved peaks at 36.95%, an equal-weight domain average; no configuration leads every domain.

hot.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
hot.summary: The authors use a diffusion model and guided search to propose factor bits for semiprimes, revising candidates and pruning partial guesses with product-based arithmetic constraints. In one test, one model-produced candidate among 15,523 held-out strict 68-bit semiprimes contained enough leading bits for lattice-based recovery. This single post-processed success does not demonstrate reliable stand-alone 68-bit factorization.

likes.title: You don't need long context
likes.summary: The authors test whether agents need full histories or documents in active context using compact handoff states and tool-based retrieval. In long-horizon and long-input tasks these approaches preserve or improve results. For Qwen 3 Coder Next, a 16K rather than 256K context window yielded 7× more decoded tokens per second; this measures throughput, not task time, and evidence is limited.

likes.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
likes.summary: TKCC enables agents to optimize inference deployments as workloads change by hot-reloading candidate forward passes in a persistent engine, screening them before representative measurements. Its cost model selects GPU-parallelism configurations. On B200 GLM 5.3, two-tier measurement evaluated 1,354 candidates versus 168 for a single slow tier and found a 7.2% faster solution; the result is specific to that comparison.

likes.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² teaches an evolver reusable guidance for changing a frozen model’s task harness during a run, rather than selecting one harness for every task. Its Meta-Skill guides when to edit, hold, or avoid changes; edits remain run-local, without held-out verifier feedback. With GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports mean@5 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and mean@3 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1, on two tested benchmarks.

likes.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The authors introduce targeted guidance for multi-turn software-engineering reinforcement learning, placing textual feedback before a failing turn and distilling the same model’s hint-conditioned token predictions only there, alongside ordinary rewards. In their coding setup, Markdown reward is 0.85 ± 0.09 versus 0.00 ± 0.00 for GRPO, while coding pass-rate is 0.33 ± 0.05 versus 0.33 ± 0.07; findings are limited to this setting and designed feedback.

likes.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
likes.summary: FrontierPhysics evaluates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended physics research from high-level briefs. The benchmark uses physicist-contributed research tasks and grades structured outputs with deterministic checks, alongside manuscripts and research trajectories against expert-authored rubrics. Passing requires all verifier tests and blocking criteria. The top tested configuration passed 46/168 trials (27.4%), measuring performance under this protocol rather than human publication acceptance.

likes.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
likes.summary: The authors test whether on-policy distillation transfers specialist improvements beyond supervised tasks. A student learns from its own responses with teacher guidance; multi-teacher training routes domains to matching teachers. Narrow math supervision nearly matches teacher scores in-distribution but leaves out-of-distribution performance 3.73% below base. Broader data with a stronger teacher raises scores across five benchmarks, but effects are not isolated.

likes.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
likes.summary: The authors use speculative decoding to steer selected decisions into less noisy context positions. A trained draft is more likely to be rejected at those points, so the target resamples at the start of a fresh verification block while preserving its token distribution. On DeepSWE, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 pass rate rises from 60.6% to 67.6%; not all benchmark gains are statistically established.

likes.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small
likes.summary: Inkling 2 Small is Thinking Machines Lab's second model generation: a 594B-total, 17B-active Mixture-of-Experts model with a 292M-parameter vision encoder and variable effort. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, launching on Tinker with closed weights ahead of a planned Apache 2.0 weight release after external safety testing. The post covers its coding, autoresearch, vision, knowledge work and alignment results alongside details of its pretraining and a single joint RL run.

likes.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
likes.summary: GSBR guides online robot learning by penalizing actions only outside neighborhoods around sampled actions from a pretrained controller. This lets the actor choose among supported behaviors while permitting nearby improvements at a distance-based cost. Across 19 tasks in four benchmarks, GSBR averages 95% success and 0.95 normalized throughput, versus RLT’s 0.77; on LIBERO, RLT has higher success.

likes.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
likes.summary: Scientist World turns empirical AI research papers into runnable environments where agents reproduce methods, set improvement targets, package tasks, and verify them. Its release contains 1,000 environments, while tests cover ten lower-compute environments. Attempts improved over reproduced methods in 84% of Improve runs and 74% of Innovate runs, measured by held-out gains; Innovate has more regressions.

likes.title: Introducing Ripple-65B Preview, a Frontier Open-Weight Model
likes.summary: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary language model that powers its AI chip design platform. The dense 65B model was trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context, and reaches 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a new U.S. open-weight state of the art for agentic coding. The full R&D cost was $32M, which the team estimates is one-tenth that of the previous open-weight SOTA.

likes.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
likes.summary: SLA teaches a vision-language-action policy spatial structure by aligning its intermediate visual features with a frozen 3D perception model during continual pre-training and task-specific post-training, without adding depth as a policy input. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, both-stage alignment reaches 72.3% success, above either single-stage alternative; this result supports the combined recipe in the tested setup, not universal causation.

likes.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
likes.summary: DreamX transfers motion from human videos to robot actions without paired human–robot training data. It uses learnable queries to read a pretrained video model’s features and compress motion into a code, which can condition future-video generation or robot action prediction. On LARYBench, it achieves 0.17 average normalized action MSE and 69.67% accuracy; transfer is demonstrated only in evaluated open-loop settings.

likes.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: ToolSpace builds executable cross-service task paths from observed tool-call traces, linking adjacent calls through data, state, and retry dependencies. It samples paths whose inputs are available, replays them from initial states, and retains those passing checks. ToolSpace-35B-A3B averages 41.0 across seven benchmarks, versus 23.0 for its backbone and 43.2 after on-policy RL; replay validates chains, not agent success.
